newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Barlow sees further earnings growth for yr.
newsitem.headline: Barlow sees further earnings growth for yr.

text.p: South African industrial holding company, Barlow Ltd, said on Monday it expected futher growth in earnings for the full year.
Commenting on prospects in a statement issued with half-year results, Barlow said it was disappointed at the lack of implementation of much-needed public sector fixed investment programmes.
But despite this the group remained positive about medium-term growth prospects for South Africa, evidenced by continued investment by its subsidiaries.
"This is evidenced by the continued investment in our subsidiaries and the group's ongoing capital expenditure programme," the industrial holding group said.
Barlow earlier posted below-expectation half year pre-exceptional earnings up to 145.4 cents from 142.5 a year ago, compared with analysts' estimates of a rise to between 150 and 165 cents.
The group said that although the local operations experienced lower margins, the international business did well improving their contribution to attributable profit to 34 percent of group earnings.

It said the offshore materials handling division saw increased sales although markets in the United Kingdom and parts of the United States did not sustain levels of lift truck deliveries. Spain and Portugal remained strong markets.

Locally, the capital equipment division produced satisfactory results with mining sector demand remaining firm. Good growth was seen in the heavy engineering unit, but materials handling was hard hit by declining sales and margins.
The paint division was mixed, while the steel tube division was squeezed by a downturn in the steel industry.
The motor vehicle retailing business was able to increase market share and maintain earnings in difficult trading conditions.
The cement and lime division, of which Pretoria Portland Cement Co Ltd is part, earlier this month reported a slide in earnings.
